summary: Horace L. Friess worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1915–1926) and Heidelberg University (~1921–1922), and held posts at Johns Hopkins University and Columbia University, where he was attested as professor in 1970.

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1999, served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995, and became a lecturer at Vienna in 1999.
Hoseok Leigh focuses on philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic posts at Koyasan University, where he was attested as a professor in 1982 and as an emeritus professor in 2004.

Houn Jiyu-Kennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Durham University (~1944–1947) and trained under traditional teachers Sek Kim Seng (~1961–1962) and Keidō Chisan Kohō (~1962–1963).

Hoyo Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1960). He later served at Rissho University as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1974–2004) and as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~1983–1995).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy. He also served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hsiang-Kuang Chou was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Swami Sivananda (attested 1960). His posts included positions at the University of Delhi, University of Allahabad, LBSNAA, and Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Hu completed a PhD at Temple University and served as an associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yin Shun (attested 1988) and at the University of Hong Kong. He held a post at National Taiwan University and founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. Lee completed a master's degree at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hsu Yun in 1948. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist University, the Buddhist Text Translation Society, and the Institute for World Religions, and served as Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaii at Hilo (~1974–2012).

Hu Shih was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Cornell, Teachers College, and Columbia (PhD 1915–1917), and held posts at Peking University (1946), Fu Jen Catholic University, and as President of Academia Sinica (1958).

Huai-Chin Nan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy (~1937–1939) and under Huanxian Yuan (~1942–1947), later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Chinese Culture University (attested 1986).

Huaiyu Chen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Chen earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong (1994), completed doctoral studies under Stephen F. Teiser (~2000–2007), and was assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2007–2013).

Huanhuan He is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and as a professor at Zhejiang University (attested 2015).
Huawen Bai was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955) and subsequently served as a professor there from ~1955 to 2000.

Hubert Decleer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He held positions at the School for International Training (1987, 1999), Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.
